title: Patchwork customer hypotheses and synthesis — Jun 2029
body:
Context / purpose:

This is a working roll-up of recent field threads (May 20 - Jun 10 2029) focused on: onboarding friction for Dedicated/Private, production quality regressions after model swaps, cost-sensitivity signals, and small but high-frequency UX asks from integrations teams. Goal: produce a short, prioritized set of hypothesis-driven experiments + quick patches that ENG/Product can pick up in the next two sprints.

Notes format: quick vignette -> observed pain -> hypothesis -> proposed probe (low-effort first) -> expected metric.

Vignette A — "LargeGov" (mid-size public sector)
- Observed pain: During early Dedicated onboarding they saw intermittent 500s when routing between regions (failover). App teams lost logs for those requests and could not reconcile what model variant served the fallback.
- Hypothesis: Smart routing fallback does not attach consistent request metadata (model_version + routing_reason) for Private/Dedicated fallback events, causing confusion and gaps in audit logs.
- Proposed probe: Add lightweight routing metadata header to all fallback responses (x-rd-route-reason, x-rd-model-variant) and a short UI toggle in Console to show recent fallback events for a deployment. Rollout as feature-flag for Dedicated customers for one week.
- Expected metric: Reduction in 'missing metadata' support tickets for fallback incidents by 70% in the test cohort; mean time to resolution (MTTR) down by 40%.

Vignette B — "Shoply" (AI-native commerce)
- Observed pain: Sudden increase in token billing after a model patch — Shoply claims output truncation led to resubmits.
- Hypothesis: Default generation settings (max_tokens + temperature) differ between model variants; platform doesn't surface delta when auto-failing to a larger model variant. Customers unknowingly get higher token usage.
- Proposed probe: Add a per-request 'effective billing multiplier' preview in logs (simple: tokens_estimated * model_multiplier) plus an opt-in safety lane that prevents auto-fallback to variants that increase per-token cost beyond a configurable threshold.
- Expected metric: Fewer surprise-billing disputes; measured token consumption delta visible in billing exports within 24h.

Vignette C — "HealthApp" (regulated, private deployment)
- Observed pain: Security team flagged that audit logs retain partial KV cache keys in plaintext in debug traces during canary experiments.
- Hypothesis: Debug traces leak sensitive cache metadata when debug_log_level >= INFO; we don't strip sensitive identifiers before storing traces in Private control plane.
- Proposed probe: Create a 'scrub' pass on exported traces for Private deployments that replaces identifiable KV key prefixes with deterministic hashes; test on one on-prem pilot customer.
- Expected metric: Security sign-off for the pilot within 10 days; zero PII exposure incidents in the pilot bucket.

Cross-cutting themes observed (synthesis):
- Metadata & observability gaps: recurring asks for clearer per-request metadata (which model variant, routing path, fallback reason). Often appears in Dedicated/Private onboarding cases.
- Cost transparency: customers want preflight / precommit warnings when routing or fallback will materially change token/unit economics.
- Lightweight guardrails: customers ask for simple toggles (prevent auto-upgrade to bigger variants, hold rollouts, require manual approval for model switches) rather than full policy engines.
- Docs + examples: Onboarding docs show ideal path but not common failure modes (e.g., prefix cache invalidation after canary). Field engineers end up writing bespoke guides; we should standardize.
- Quick UX wins: console-level recent-fallback feed, per-deployment 'cost delta preview', per-request trace view with scrubbed KV keys.

Quick patch / experiment backlog (ranked):
1) Routing metadata header + Console fallback feed (low effort): engineering + console (2 wk). Flag: enabled for Dedicated pilots only. Owner: Diego.
2) Cost-delta preview in logs + safety toggle preventing cost-increasing fallbacks (medium): product + billing + routing (3 wk). Owner: Jasleen.
3) Trace scrubbing pass for Private (high priority for regulated): infra + security (2 wk sprint + 1 week pilot). Owner: Liam.
4) Onboarding failure-mode playbook (doc + 3 runbooks): docs + SE (1 wk). Owner: Maya.
5) SDK example repo: explicit model-variant pinning patterns + token estimation helper (low). Owner: solutions-eng.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should fallbacks be 'cost-aware' by default? Pros: fewer surprises. Cons: could reduce availability for SLA-critical apps. Need product policy for customer tier mapping.
- For Private/on-prem scrubbing: do we hash deterministic or salt per-customer? Deterministic hashing helps debug across teams; salted hashes increase privacy. Security prefers salted. Decision needed.
- How to signal to users that a rollback occurred due to cost vs capacity; separate flags?

Customer micro-asks (small, fast wins):
- Console: 'Show last 10 model variants that served this route' (UI card) — low effort, ship in 1 sprint.
- API: faster way to pin model_version in request without needing full deployment (query param preview) — tiny SDK change.
- Billing CSV: add 'effective_model' column that indicates which variant actually served the request.

Metrics to monitor for probes:
- Support ticket count for 'billing surprise' / 'fallback confusion' (CS triage tag).
- MTTR for production incidents involving model swaps.
- Fraction of requests served by fallback variants.
- Privacy audit results (traces) pre/post scrub.

Next immediate actions (owner + ETA):
- Diego: prototype routing metadata headers and Console feed (demo by 2029-06-21).
- Jasleen: run quick stakeholder alignment with Billing & Routing (meeting 2029-06-16), prepare spec.
- Liam: draft trace scrubbing design and threat model (draft by 2029-06-18).
- Maya: produce onboarding failure-mode playbook skeleton and collect SE-run examples (2029-06-20).

Notes to self / loose fragments:
- We should include a tiny flag in the hosted API 'cost_guard=threshold' that refuses fallbacks that exceed threshold; could be an early alpha.
- Consider exposing 'routing_reason' histogram on per-route dashboard (high signal for ops).
- There are ~6 customers with overlapping asks; combine them into a 'fallback transparency' pilot.

Raw snippets from field threads (unedited):
- "We had 3 incident pages in a day when the model swapped and our validation bot started submitting 5x the tokens — billing surprised us."
- "When we open a ticket the logs only say 'fallback occurred' — we need the model name or we spend hours guessing."
- "Can we opt out of automatic model upgrades? We want to test ourselves before switching in prod."

Attachments to add (follow-up):
- export of CS tickets tagged 'fallback' (last 60 days) -> link (todo)
- list of Dedicated customers on recent rollouts -> internal sheet (todo)

Decision log stub (for later):
- 2029-06-14: agree to pilot routing metadata header + console feed for Dedicated. Responsible: Diego.

End.
